events.desc: The drawing room. Clara by the window, puzzle piece in hand. Hartwell has moved. Danny watches from the door.
events.thinking:
**My ears find Danny before my eyes do.** He is near the door — the only door — and his weight is settled, not passing through. My hearing maps the room in the same breath: Tommy's breathing by the fireplace, Sparks shifting at the window, the specific quality of Danny's stillness that says he is watching something he has not yet named. The fine hairs on my forearms lift. Three positions. Three sight lines. My fingertips catalogue the geometry without my gaze leaving the centre of the room — Danny to door, Tommy to hearth, Sparks to window — and the exits narrow to one, behind the one who is watching me, and my peripheral vision holds all three of them the way my hands hold a combination lock, each tumbler's position known before I've decided what to do with the knowing.

**Clara turns the puzzle piece and her brow furrows.** Something warm and unhurried fills my chest — not the self-preservation prickling along my forearms, not the fingertips' angular mapping. Lower, heavier, behind the sternum: the slow heat of watching someone reach for something they will never find without me. Her fingers press too hard against the edges. She is trying to solve it the way she tries to solve everything — earnestly, beautifully, wrong. My jaw loosens into the warmth. Time stretches around this watching, and I want to stay inside it, want every second of her concentrated, trusting failing to sit a little longer in my chest. At twelve I found the mechanism — the right words, the right smile — and the sweetest part was always the gap between what they saw and what I held. That gap is here now, filling my sternum, warm and patient. My fingers stay still at my sides. Pemberton's hands, helpful, open. The performance costs nothing when the warmth is this good.

**But Hartwell has moved.** My attention catches it the way a tripwire catches weight — not the action itself but the architecture behind it. He is standing between Clara and the corridor. Not beside her. Between. He read the narrow passage, the blind corner, the single exit, and he rerouted her without saying why. My jaw sets. The belief I held — predictable, earnest, a wall to route around — cracks along a line I didn't know was there. Something old tightens in my spine, the correction that predates Pemberton, the one that arrives when the room doesn't organise the way it should. He is not just protective. He is observant. My weight redistributes — lower, wider, the body's preparation for a controlled environment becoming less controlled. My ears sharpen beneath the jaw's tightening, tracking his breathing, the angle of his stance, whether his attention has shifted from Clara to me. It hasn't. Not yet. But the margin narrowed, and I feel it in my fingertips — the geometry of the room recalculating, each angle adjusting around this new variable, the plan's architecture absorbing the revision the way a bridge absorbs a heavier load.

**Foxworth narrates to no one.** His fingers hover near the portrait gilding and my attention registers him the way it registers furniture — position, utility, weight. My fingertips file him into the periphery without spending a heartbeat: he will go where I point him, he will touch what I suggest, he will carry blame the way a mule carries salt. The dismissal settles into my shoulders as a particular kind of ease — no energy required, no recalculation needed. He is already where he belongs in the geometry.

**My spine holds its vertical.** Danny watches. Hartwell recalculates. Clara trusts. And beneath all of it — beneath the sternum's warmth, beneath the jaw's tightening, beneath the fingertips' angular revision — my ears hold the room, counting breaths, tracking the creak of Tommy's weight on the hearthstone, the silence from Sparks that means he is looking at something, the distance between Danny's stillness and the door handle. Twenty years of this house in my body. They have been here forty minutes. My spine does not bend.
